title: How to Grow on Pinterest in 2026 (Try these NEW tools!)
key_points: Tailwind is an approved partner of Pinterest that the creator has used since 2019 for scheduling pins

Schedulers do not negatively impact Pinterest pin distribution - the creator has tested pins published via Tailwind, Pinterest's native scheduler, and live pinning with no drastic difference in overall performance
Consistency is identified as a pillar of Pinterest marketing strategy alongside keywords and scroll-stopping pins
Pinterest is a search engine, not social media, making keyword research essential for growth
Audiences include both problem-aware and solution-aware people who use different keywords based on where they are in their journey
Tailwind Turbo Pin is a new feature (still in beta) that encourages reciprocal engagement between Pinterest creators using Tailwind
Turbo Pin requires 10 engagements with other users' pins (likes, comments, or saves) before you can submit your next pin to the Turbo feed
The creator's one Turbo Pin submitted on December 5th achieved 521 impressions, 11 engagements, and 1 save, becoming their best performing pin in the past 30 days
Tailwind's free keyword tool allows users to enter either a keyword or a web page URL to find related top keywords on Pinterest
The keyword tool shows 'resonance' (relevance to search and actively promoted by Pinterest) and Pinterest search volume for select keywords
Pinterest only shares search volume for select keywords, so resonance should be used to compare reach when volume data isn't available
Keywords can be saved in the Tailwind tool and associated with specific URLs for organization
The outdated practice of saving 80% other people's pins and 20% your own is incorrect - Pinterest has confirmed you can save 100% your own content
Saving other people's pins to your boards is not necessary for your Pinterest marketing strategy and Pinterest has confirmed this
Pin Clicks is mentioned as another fantastic keyword research tool for Pinterest with a separate video available
Tailwind communities are different from Turbo Pins - communities focus on engaging with like-minded people within your niche, while Turbo Pins don't require niche relevance
Monthly reporting for Pinterest management should track reach, saves, outbound clicks, and year-over-year account growth rather than just month-over-month
The creator recommends storing pillar and longtail keywords in a working document like Google Sheets or Airtable for use in pins, titles, descriptions, account bio, and profile name
summary:
This video covers two new Tailwind tools for Pinterest marketing in 2026. The creator begins by addressing a common misconception about whether schedulers negatively impact Pinterest pin distribution. She states she has used Tailwind since 2019 as a Pinterest manager and has tested pins published via Tailwind versus Pinterest's native scheduler versus live pinning, finding no drastic difference in overall performance. She emphasizes that lazy practices when using schedulers, rather than the schedulers themselves, cause poor results. She creates monthly reports for clients tracking reach, saves, outbound clicks, and year-over-year growth.

The creator explains that Pinterest is fundamentally a search engine, not social media, making keywords critical. She notes that audiences include both problem-aware and solution-aware people who search using different keywords depending on where they are in their journey. Consistency is identified as another pillar of Pinterest marketing strategy alongside keywords and scroll-stopping pins. She mentions that Tailwind is an approved partner of Pinterest.

The first new tool demonstrated is Tailwind Turbo Pin, currently in beta. This feature encourages reciprocal engagement between Pinterest creators using Tailwind. Users must engage with other users' pins (through likes, comments, or saves) to earn credits for submitting their own pins. The system requires 10 engagements before you can submit your next pin. The creator shows her Turbo feed, which displays various pins not necessarily related to her niche, and demonstrates engaging with food-related pins. She shows her one submitted Turbo Pin from December 5th achieved 521 impressions, 11 engagements, and 1 save, noting it became her best performing pin in the past 30 days, though she strategically chose a pin she felt would perform well organically.

The creator addresses an outdated Pinterest practice, stating that the old advice of saving 80% other people's pins and 20% your own is incorrect. Pinterest has confirmed users can save 100% their own content. She clarifies that with Turbo Pins, you can engage through likes and comments rather than saving pins to your boards.

The second tool is Tailwind's free keyword research tool. This tool allows users to enter either a keyword or a web page URL to discover related top keywords on Pinterest. The interface shows keyword resonance (relevance to search and active Pinterest promotion) and Pinterest search volume for select keywords. The creator demonstrates by entering her blog post URL about becoming a Pinterest manager, which generates keywords like Pinterest manager course, Pinterest manager services, Pinterest manager jobs, and Pinterest virtual assistant jobs. She notes that Pinterest only shares search volume for select keywords, so resonance should be used when volume data isn't available. Keywords can be saved and associated with specific URLs within the tool. She recommends storing pillar and longtail keywords in Google Sheets or Airtable for use in pins, titles, descriptions, account bio, and profile name. She also mentions Pin Clicks as another keyword research tool for Pinterest.
